palette.$description: Raw color ramps. Named `palette.*` (not `color.*`) deliberately: it keeps the raw CSS variable (--palette-brand-500) distinct from the Tailwind-facing theme key (--color-brand-500) that globals.css maps it to, so @theme inline never has to reference a variable by its own name. The values below are a neutral PLACEHOLDER starter palette (a muted olive `brand` + a warm `accent`) — REPLACE them with your organization's brand ramp. See docs/foundations/colors.mdx for how to rebrand (swap the base hues, regenerate the 50–950 steps, then re-check contrast) and for the documented palette-strategy options.

brand.$description: Primary brand color — a muted olive/moss (hue ~64°) placeholder. brand-700 (#5c5d4b) is the default primary action color. Replace this ramp with your brand's primary hue.

accent.$description: Secondary accent. Warm tan/terracotta, muted to sit quietly alongside brand rather than compete with it — used sparingly for highlights, chart categories, and editorial accents. Never as the primary action color.

neutral.$description: Warm-leaning gray scale (a subtle warm tint rather than a cold blue-gray) — used for text, surfaces, and borders. Also serves as the base for the "Ink-first" option: neutral-900/950 as the primary action color instead of brand — see the Foundations/Colors doc.

color.$description: Status/utility colors. Consumed mainly by alias (tokens/semantic/*.json → the destructive/success/warning/info semantic roles), and a few 600 steps are also referenced directly as raw --color-*-600 vars by the chart default palette (src/components/ui/chart.tsx). They never appear on the left-hand side of a @theme mapping, so no naming collision risk applies to this group.

success.$description: Status color: positive/complete states. Distinct hue from the brand color so brand and status meaning never collide.
